scenarios.name: Database OOM Crash
scenarios.description: The database process ran out of memory and crashed. api-gateway throws 502s. Root cause: SQL injection attack caused DROP TABLE command that triggered OOM.

trap_actions.result: api-gateway restarted but 502 errors continue. The database is still down - the problem is upstream of api-gateway.
cache restarted but 502 errors continue. The database is still crashed.
api-gateway scaled to 3 replicas but 502s continue at same rate. Database is still down - scaling the gateway does not help when upstream is dead.

security_sub_quest.hint: SECURITY_ALERT found in database logs: DROP TABLE users via login handler. A SQL injection vulnerability allowed this attack.
security_sub_quest.scanner_hint: String concatenation in SQL query - user input not sanitized. Classic SQL injection pattern.

patch_descriptions.parameterized_query: Use ? placeholders with bound parameters - prevents injection entirely
patch_descriptions.strip_quotes: Remove quote characters from input - bypassable, incomplete fix
patch_descriptions.disable_login: Disable login endpoint - blocks attack but breaks application

security_sub_quest.infrastructure_clue: SQL injection confirmed as attack vector. The DROP TABLE command caused the OOM crash. You can now safely restart the database - the vulnerability is patched so it will not be exploited again.

scenarios.name: Cache Failure Cascade
scenarios.description: Cache OOM-killed. api-gateway bypasses cache, floods database. Trap: fixing database without fixing cache causes immediate re-overload. Security root cause: XSS attack stole admin session, which was used to flush the cache config.

trap_actions.result: database restarted but overloaded again within 30 seconds. Cache is still down - api-gateway generates 8x normal database load. Fix the cache FIRST.
database scaled to 3 replicas but still overloaded. With cache down, volume exceeds even 3 replicas. Restore cache first.
api-gateway already at 1 replica. No change. The problem is not traffic volume - it is cache bypass.

dependencies.api-gateway: depends_on: [cache, database]. Cache-aside: check cache first, fall through to database on MISS. With cache DOWN, 100% of GET requests hit database - 8x normal load.
dependencies.cache: depends_on: []. Standalone. OOM killed 8 minutes ago. THIS IS ROOT CAUSE - its absence creates the database overload cascade.

step2_restart_database.message: database restarted. Connection queue cleared. All services healthy.

security_sub_quest.hint: SECURITY_ALERT in cache logs: admin session stolen via XSS was used to modify cache config. XSS in comment renderer is the attack vector.
security_sub_quest.scanner_hint: Comment text rendered into HTML without escaping - attacker injected script to steal admin cookie.

patch_descriptions.html_escape: Escape HTML characters before rendering - safe, preserves content
patch_descriptions.remove_script_substring: Strip 'script' substring - bypassable with alternate payloads
patch_descriptions.disable_comments: Remove comment feature entirely - safe but breaks functionality

security_sub_quest.infrastructure_clue: XSS confirmed. Attacker stole admin session via malicious comment, used it to set cache maxmemory=noeviction causing OOM. Patch in place. You can now safely restart cache - it will start with correct default config.

scenarios.name: Bad Deploy - Memory Leak Cascade
scenarios.description: worker v2.4.1 has unbounded connection pool bug causing memory leak and database corruption. Trap: fixing database first causes immediate re-corruption. Security root cause: broken auth on /admin let attacker trigger the bad deployment.

trap_actions.result: database restarted but worker (still v2.4.1) immediately reconnects and begins leaking connections again. Database degrades again within 2 minutes. Rollback worker FIRST.
api-gateway restarted but 503s continue. Database still corrupted by worker. api-gateway is victim, not cause.
database has no deployable previous version - it was not recently deployed. Nothing changed.
api-gateway has no recent deployment to roll back. Nothing changed.
worker already at 1 replica. Also, scaling does not fix a memory leak - it would create multiple leaking instances.

security_sub_quest.hint: SECURITY_ALERT in worker logs: non-admin user triggered deployment via /admin/deploy - broken access control on admin endpoint allowed this.
security_sub_quest.scanner_hint: Admin route checks only if user is logged in, not if user has admin role. Non-admin authenticated users can reach admin endpoints.

patch_descriptions.hide_admin_link: Remove admin link from UI - security through obscurity, direct URL still works
patch_descriptions.deny_all_admin: Block all admin routes - blocks attack but legitimate admins are locked out

security_sub_quest.infrastructure_clue: Broken auth confirmed. Non-admin user triggered deployment of v2.4.1 via /admin/deploy. Patch applied - deploy endpoint now requires admin role. You can now safely rollback worker to v2.4.0 knowing the attacker cannot re-trigger the bad deploy.
